title: AI weather models struggle to predict unprecedented extreme weather events
independence: primary study; model comparison and record benchmark
limits: record threshold is training-history/reanalysis based; 2018/2020 and selected models; gridded truth; spatial duplicates; no operational replacement test

title: Can data-driven models beat numerical weather prediction models in predicting extreme events?
independence: separate study and authorship; model families overlap but outcome benchmark is independent
limits: top-1/top-5-percentile extremes rather than strict records; 1.5-degree common grid; not a direct replication

title: Assessing deep learning weather forecasts for extreme events
independence: separate case-study analysis; some author/literature overlap with primary field
limits: three events, not global population; humidity-variable limitation in one case; case-study estimands

title: WeatherBench 2 official evaluation data and repository
independence: data infrastructure; not counted as an outcome study
limits: public coarse grid and model data do not reproduce every paper checkpoint or 0.25-degree event table

title: A physically consistent graph neural network for weather prediction
independence: separate technical method; not an independent global extreme ranking
limits: proof-of-principle; deterministic; case studies and selected variables; not operational

title: Machine learning for numerical weather prediction
independence: review source; cited underlying studies not re-counted as separate evidence
limits: review-level synthesis; no direct estimate for the R2 benchmark

title: RealBench: Real-world evaluation of weather foundation models
independence: new benchmark proposal; no validated outcome used here
limits: preprint; full artifact not independently validated in this audit

title: NWP-Benchmark
